yield_rationale: Substrate-honest assessment: JRPG/isekai holy vocabulary IS dominated by proper-nouns (Hama family) and mechanical-keywords (Cure/Cura/Esuna/Reflect/Banish/Resurrection/Holy Smite/Greater Heal) as gandalf's substrate-honest-WEAK caveat anticipated. However, the substrate is NOT as thin as the most pessimistic expectation: the Hama tier-structure deepening (Hamaon/Mahama/Mahamaon) adds 3 novel proper-noun rows; the Mushoku Tensei healing tier + Overlord divine-class system adds 5 novel mechanical-keyword rows; and 3 non-proper-noun non-mechanical-keyword candidates emerged (lux, celestial, radiance-recited). Total: 12 novel rows. Substrate-honest-WEAK did NOT fire because the yield exceeded the 'no novel non-proper-noun, non-mechanical-keyword vocabulary beyond aura/seraph variants' threshold — lux and celestial are novel non-proper-noun non-mechanical-keyword candidates (material and phenomenon respectively). However, yield is genuinely thinner than other elements; the dominant substrate is mechanical-keyword territory. Setting MEDIUM not STRONG to reflect substrate-honest assessment.

source_coverage_breadth.notes: FF White Magic provides the most canonical JRPG holy mechanical-keyword vocabulary: Cure/Cura/Curaga, Esuna, Reflect, Banish, Holy. This is the deepest holy vocabulary source in JRPG.
Hama tier deepened to full four-tier sequence: Hama(Phase1)/Hamaon/Mahama/Mahamaon. All are proper-noun holy insta-kill spells mirroring the Mudo shadow family.

Overlord divine-class system yields Holy Smite, Greater Heal, Resurrection framing. All are mechanical-keywords. The divine-class tier vocabulary (Lower/Middle/Higher Tier) is structural but the sub-vocabulary remains mechanical.
Healing magic tiers confirm Cure/Resurrection naming conventions. Lux as light-energy root is the most novel contribution from Mushoku Tensei. Thin beyond tier-vocabulary.
Black Clover contributes to radiance citation but no new candidates beyond FF/SMT vocabulary. Re:Zero and KonoSuba healing vocabulary yields no candidates beyond what FF already covers.

substrate_tagging_observations: JRPG/isekai holy substrate is structurally bifurcated: proper-nouns (Hama family, Holy-as-spell-name, Seraph/Aura mythological entities) and mechanical-keywords (Cure family, Esuna, Reflect, Banish, Holy Smite, Greater Heal, Resurrection). Non-proper-noun non-mechanical-keyword vocabulary surfaced: lux (Latin light-material), celestial (astronomical phenomenon), radiance (light-emission phenomenon). These 3 candidates are the genuine flavor-substrate results of the expansion. The rest is proper-noun and mechanical-keyword domain. This is a substrate-honest finding: JRPG/isekai genre DOES treat holy as primarily action-mechanical (what holy magic DOES: heals, purifies, smites, resurrects) rather than phenomenon-substrate (what holy IS in material/phenomenal terms).
expansion_sub_agent_summary: JRPG/isekai × holy Phase 3 expansion: substrate-honest-WEAK DID NOT fire (12 novel candidates surfaced, exceeding the 'no novel non-proper-noun, non-mechanical-keyword beyond aura/seraph variants' threshold). However, yield is thinner than fire/water/shadow, and the dominant pattern IS proper-noun + mechanical-keyword as gandalf anticipated. Yield distribution: proper-nouns = 6 of 16 rows (Hamaon, Mahama, Mahamaon, Seraph-re-cited, Aura-re-cited, Holy Smite); mechanical-keywords = 8 of 16 rows (Cure, Cura, Esuna, Reflect, Banish, Resurrection, Holy Smite, Greater Heal); non-proper-noun non-mechanical-keyword flavor-substrate = 3 of 16 rows (lux, celestial, radiance). Setting yield_score MEDIUM: not WEAK because novel candidates did emerge and flavor-substrate is not zero; not STRONG because the dominant character of the substrate remains mechanical-keyword territory. Top non-religious-coded flavor-substrate candidates for Phase 5a synthesis: lux(1), celestial(2), radiance(3). Note: substrate-honest-WEAK status per gandalf amendment is borderline — Phase 5a synthesis should be aware that lux and celestial are thin-cited (2 citations each) and may require cross-track confirmation before promotion to the allow-list.
